examples.title: SaaS Free-Trial Removal
examples.problem: B2B CRM software company facing low conversion rates (2%) from free trials due to customer setup inertia.
examples.assets: Software code, sales team, customer support, user onboarding process, customer data.
examples.perception: A free trial is mandatory to convince buyers to test features before paying.
examples.manipulation: Remove the 14-day self-service free trial completely.
examples.concept: A high-friction software sign-up flow with no self-service access, requiring upfront commitment.
examples.adaptation: Eliminated trial tire-kickers. Replaced trial with a 30-minute personalized ROI consultation and mandatory live onboarding upon payment.
examples.results: Conversion rate jumped from 2% to 18%, average deal size increased 40%, customer lifetime value doubled due to proper onboarding.

examples.title: Retail Store Cashier Elimination
examples.problem: Urban convenience store struggling with high cashier wage overhead and long checkout lines during morning rush hours.
examples.assets: Store inventory, shelf sensors, cameras, mobile app, store floor, customers.
examples.perception: Every retail transaction requires a human cashier or self-checkout barcode scanning terminal.
examples.manipulation: Subtract the cashier and physical checkout terminals from the store environment.
examples.concept: A retail store where customers walk in, grab items, and exit directly through the door with zero checkout interaction.
examples.adaptation: Sensors and mobile app tracking bill the customer's account automatically upon exit (Grab-and-Go model).
examples.results: Reduced labor overhead by 65%, increased morning rush throughput by 300%, expanded store operating hours to 24/7.

examples.title: E-Commerce Packaging Subtraction

examples.manipulation: Subtract the outer cardboard shipping box completely.
examples.concept: A shipping label stuck directly onto the item's reusable protective inner bag.
examples.adaptation: Engineered heavy-duty, tamper-evident recycled polymer shipping bags that serve as both garment protection and outer shipping container.
examples.results: Lowered packaging unit costs by 70%, reduced shipping volume weight by 35%, improved customer brand sustainability rating.

examples.title: Restaurant Menu Subtraction

examples.adaptation: Fixed nightly multi-course tasting menu curated daily based on seasonal market availability.
examples.results: Food waste dropped to near 0%, kitchen prep time reduced by 50%, gross food margins expanded by 28% while creating an exclusive dining experience.

examples.title: Course Price Depends on Completion
examples.problem: Students buy courses and never finish them, then ask for refunds.
examples.assets: Course videos, quizzes, payment system.
examples.perception: The course price is paid once at the start.
examples.manipulation: Make part of the price depend on completion: finishers get money back.
examples.concept: A course that pays you to finish it.
examples.adaptation: A deposit is returned as credit when the final quiz is passed.
examples.results: Completion rates doubled and refund requests fell.

examples.title: Taxi Seat Price Depends on Shared Riders
examples.problem: Shuttles run half empty while single riders find taxis too expensive.
examples.assets: Shuttles, app, drivers, routes.
examples.perception: Each ride has a fixed price.
examples.manipulation: Make each rider's price depend on how many people share the ride.
examples.concept: A shuttle that gets cheaper as it fills.
examples.adaptation: The app shows the price going down as more riders join.
examples.results: Shuttles became fuller and price-sensitive riders came back.

examples.title: Hair Salon Price Depends on Stylist Level
examples.problem: Junior stylists have empty chairs while senior stylists are booked weeks ahead.
examples.assets: Stylists, booking system, price list.
examples.perception: All haircuts cost the same.
examples.manipulation: Make the price depend on the stylist's level.
examples.concept: A salon with junior, senior and master prices.
examples.adaptation: Booking shows levels and prices; juniors build their clients faster.
examples.results: All chairs filled, and senior stylists earned more per hour.

examples.title: Electricity Use Depends on Machine Load
examples.problem: Machines run on standby for hours, using power without producing.
examples.assets: Machines, sensors, production schedule.
examples.perception: Machines stay on during the whole shift.
examples.manipulation: Make machine power depend on the production queue.
examples.concept: A factory where idle machines switch to sleep mode.
examples.adaptation: Sensors switch machines down when the queue is empty and warm them up before the next job.
examples.results: Energy bills fell by about 15% with no loss of output.

examples.title: Tour Content Depends on Weather
examples.problem: Rainy days cause cancellations and refunds.
examples.assets: Guides, routes, museums, buses, customers.
examples.perception: A tour follows one fixed route.
examples.manipulation: Make the route depend on the weather.
examples.concept: A tour with a sunny version and a rainy version.
examples.adaptation: Rainy days switch to covered markets and museums; customers are told the night before.
examples.results: Cancellations on rainy days fell by about 70%.

examples.title: Newspaper Content Depends on the Reader's Town
examples.problem: Readers from different towns skip most of the paper because it is not about them.
examples.assets: Reporters, website, app, local news.
examples.perception: Every reader gets the same front page.
examples.manipulation: Make the front page depend on the reader's town.
examples.concept: A paper whose first stories are local to each reader.
examples.adaptation: The app asks the town once; local stories go to the top.
examples.results: Daily readers and subscriptions rose.
